plain: Establishes the necessary roles of admissibility, standing, reference and irreversibility. Independently warranted answers to the same complete question about the same object agree, while later repair leaves the original trial intact.
scope: Kernel governance is necessary for non-degenerate determinate objects and incidences. Conservation compares independently warranted answers about the same bearer and complete determinate question. Later evidence can correct an account; later repair cannot replace the original occurrence or conditions. A complete record also retains the substantive information required by the task.
title: Non-Degenerate Construction and the Kernel of Admissibility

plain: Shows why labels cannot recover a lost connection to the original target, and how a grounded record can supply the missing information. Distinguishes what a description tells us from which individual it can identify.
scope: The AMetric boundary is an order-of-qualification constraint. Equality-only symmetry permits equality information but supplies no privileged individual. A grounded selection needs the required input association and warrant. Complete interfaces preserve all declared uses and operation domains; these authority conditions do not describe a physical transmission mechanism.
title: The AMetric Boundary as a Unique Regime-Invariant Constraint on Admissibility-Bearing Construction

plain: Two configurations can both pass one test and still behave differently on the next. Constructs the complete information needed for the declared uses and the greatest set that remains qualified throughout them.
scope: Qualification is binary for one complete question; the full record can preserve many distinctions. The safe interior is constructed from independently fixed qualification, permitted uses and their warrants. It can contain several configurations or be empty. Safety does not by itself establish eventual completion.
title: The Structure of Admissibility

plain: Builds the complete safe set from independently specified requirements and permitted continuations. Every sound candidate set lies inside this greatest interior, and faithful descriptions preserve it even when several configurations qualify.
scope: The greatest sound interior is constructed before its membership supplies robust standing. Exact descriptions preserve local qualification and the required continuation information. One complete interior can contain many occupants; one unique occupant needs additional identity-separating constraints and a positive realization.
title: Unus Solus Possibilis Est (Uniqueness)

plain: Separates the conditions a description depends on, the meaningful content it preserves, and its presentation. These are called Anchor, Tensor and Skin.
scope: Unique fixed-domain role decomposition, importing intrinsic detectability, bivalence, fail-closure and structural exhaustion. Tensor does not necessarily mean a numerical array; anchor is not a physical mechanism.
title: Anchor, Tensor, and Skin: A Fixed-Domain Decomposition Theorem for Admissible Description (Normal Form Capstone)

plain: Asks where any genuinely different contribution could enter the same construction. Reduces relevant variation to its effect on the boundary, classification, identity or continuation.
scope: Theoremic, non-enumerative fixed-domain exhaustion via future-behavior quotient and boundary factorization. Does not exhaust arbitrary richer domains or derive physical dynamics by checking examples.
title: A Fixed-Domain Exhaustion Theorem

plain: Even rejecting every candidate requires a stable criterion and a way to identify what was evaluated. Develops the structure forced by meaningful evaluation without inferring that an admitted object exists.
scope: Governance non-vacuity from non-degenerate reuse-relevant evaluability. An all-rejecting finite model explicitly separates the required bundle from nonempty admission or concrete ontology.
title: Constraint-Bundle Forcing under Fixed-Domain Evaluability

plain: When otherwise matching descriptions cannot pick out a unique target, a declared, stable connection can fix the role without selecting the most appealing outcome.
scope: Singleton bivalent outcome-independent trace within the declared domain. Missing, multiple or unstable traces fail closed. Role fixation is not empirical confirmation and is not transmission across the AMetric boundary.
title: Boundary-Trace Fixation under Admissibility

plain: Carries the same-target requirement into differentiation: account for changes in the frame of comparison rather than confusing them with changes in the object. Develops transport, covariant differentiation and metric-compatible closure.
scope: Necessary transport-comparison role; covariant derivative in the smooth finite-linear first-jet branch. Levi-Civita follows in the stated minimal natural metric branch. No numerical connection, gauge group or complete physical model is selected by the Kernel alone.
title: Covariant Differentiation from the AASC Kernel

plain: Clarifies why the AMetric boundary is not a place where signals, objects or information pass from one side to another.
scope: A non-operational, non-transmissive constraint interface. Interface is explanatory language, not a license for adjacency, mediation or crossing.
title: SA_2 The AMetric Boundary as Non Transmissive Interface

plain: Separates the conditions for a description to count from the operations available within an already licensed description.
scope: Pre-admissible classification is not an execution process. Operators and composition require licensed interior standing; no boundary operation or same-lineage repair.
title: The AMetric Boundary Admissibility Constraint Map Paper II

plain: Explains why a purported deeper selector cannot ground the boundary by quietly reintroducing the very structure the boundary excludes.
scope: A corollary under the already fixed AMetric architecture. A proposed deeper invariant imports forbidden structure, does no governance work, or renames existing admissibility and standing.
title: The Impossibility of Deeper Invariants Under the AMetric Boundary
